what_happened: In job 1eza, the user corrected Athena's first reading before work began. The reading had a CI job running a command over the athena/records branch (criterion 7). The user said actions/checkout fetches only the triggering ref, so the branch would be missing in CI. The CI job must fetch athena/records explicitly after a full-history checkout, for example `git fetch origin athena/records:athena/records`. The command must read the branch from the ref it fetched. The user asked for this to be added to criterion 7 and left the rest of the reading as it was.
cause: The reading stage works from the request text and the local repo view. It does not ask which refs exist in the environment where the check will run. A local working copy has athena/records, but a CI checkout fetches only the triggering ref, and nothing makes the reading state how the input gets there. Criteria for a CI command are therefore written as if local state were present. The criterion would pass in a local test and fail in CI. This is related to the earlier boundary and empty-case gaps for the records walk (teks), but the cause differs: the gap is the runtime environment, not the walk's bounds.
prevention: Add a reading-stage rule that any criterion about a command run in CI must name where each input comes from in that environment. For any ref other than the triggering one, the criterion must require an explicit fetch step. Back it with a code check on the workflow file: if a CI step invokes the records check, the workflow must contain a fetch of athena/records before it. The command should also fail with a clear message, not pass silently, when the ref is absent.
proposed_request: Update the CI workflow that runs the landing-records check so it works in a fresh checkout. After actions/checkout with full history (fetch-depth: 0), add a step that runs `git fetch origin athena/records:athena/records`. The check command must read the branch from that fetched ref. If the branch is missing on the remote, the command must say so and do nothing, as already decided for the empty case. Add a test or workflow check that fails if the fetch step is missing or comes after the check step. Keep every other criterion of the current reading unchanged.
